dedupe_keys.name: opensignal mobile and broadband network experience analytics

description: Opensignal measures the connectivity that consumers actually experience on mobile and broadband networks and sells the results to operators, regulators, analysts and app developers. Coverage: global, from the company's own collection methods, which it describes as proprietary and transparent; products run from executive scorecards and public validation of network experience, through pinpoint-level engineering analytics for network technical teams, to consumer decision dynamics such as switching between carriers; for regulators it offers quality-of-service comparisons within a country and against global benchmarks. The company is headquartered in the United States with offices in the United Kingdom, Canada, continental Europe and Asia. Format and access: commercial analytics products and public reports; the reports page answered with a bot check from the cloud, so the public reports and the methodology page were not read. Licence: commercial; not read. Caveats: measurements come from users' devices, so coverage follows where the collecting apps are installed; the metrics, spatial resolution and history in the paid products were not checked; the register lists Opensignal together with Ookla, but no ownership statement was read. Simulation uses: observed network speed, availability and coverage experience for telecom service performance baselines and resilience studies of mobile networks. Related records: Speedtest by Ookla open performance tiles (data-ookla-open-data-performance-tiles) and Mexico's crowdsourced 4G coverage maps (data-ift-crowdsourced-4g-coverage-maps-mexico).
